Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.4675 Of 2019
Order:

The petitioners/A1 and A2 seek to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.223 of 2019 of Eluru Rural Police Station, West Godavari District, which was registered against them for the offence under Sections 328, 270 and 273 of IPC and Section 22 of Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production,
Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 (for short, 'COTP Act, 2003').
2.

sentences.text: The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that on 01.08.2019 at 11.30 P.M., the complainant on receiving the credible information proceeded to JMJ School, Tangellamudi Panchyat, Eluru Mandal and found a container lorry having Registration No. NL 01AA 6326 stationed on the Eluru- Jangareddigudem road and some bags were transported into a truck auto having Registration No. AP 39Y 1168 and on seeing the police, when the persons in the vehicles were tried to skulk away, then the police arrested A1 and A2 and on the revelation, they came to know that they were transporting 30 bags of Khaini and A1 allegedly confessed that on instructions of A3 he loaded 30 bags of Khaini in the lorry and they bound to deliver them at Eluru.

Hence, the FIR is registered for the offences under Sections 328, 270 and 273 of IPC and Section 22 of COTP Act,
2003.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution is accepted to be true, the Khaini is a tobacco product would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of Food Safety Standards Act (for short, 'FSS Act') and therefore, the police are not authorized to register the crime and investigation and file charge sheet and therefore,
registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.

As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and only quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act, whereas permitted the respondents to proceed against the petitioners therein for the offences punishable under the provisions of COTP Act.

4. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is partly allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioner under Sections 328, 270 and 273 IPC are hereby quashed and the respondents are permitted to proceed against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Section 22 of COTP Act.
